config.title: Inline Styles

intro.title: Inline Styles
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple React component that applies custom styling directly to HTML elements using inline styles. You'll learn how to use the style attribute in JSX to set CSS properties as JavaScript objects, controlling the appearance of your UI programmatically. The main technologies involved are React, JSX, and JavaScript objects for styling. This approach is a foundational way to add dynamic styles to your components without external CSS files.
intro.usecase: Inline styles are commonly used in React for dynamic styling that changes based on user interactions or application state. For example, in a dashboard with real-time metrics, you might use inline styles to change the color of a progress bar as values update, or highlight form fields with validation errors in red. This approach is also practical for creating interactive components like collapsible panels where you need to dynamically set height or visibility, or for implementing drag-and-drop interfaces where element positions change programmatically. While CSS classes are better for static styling, inline styles excel when visual properties must be computed or updated on the fly.

objectives: Apply inline styles to React elements using the style attribute
Construct style objects with JavaScript syntax and camelCase property names
Initialize dynamic style values by binding them to component state variables
Manipulate style properties conditionally based on component props or state
Integrate inline styles with event handlers to create interactive UI elements
Render components with combined static and dynamic inline styling approaches
Configure responsive inline styles that update when user interactions occur
